summary: Frontier legend Jim Bowie laundered smuggled Africans into the US slave market, ran vast land frauds in Louisiana, Arkansas and Mexican Texas, killed a man in the Sandbar Fight and died at the Alamo in 1836.

evidence.note: Birth in Logan County, Kentucky, given as 1796, with the year flagged as uncertain
Joins James Long's 1819 filibuster into Texas, his first major venture
Bowie brothers launder slaves bought from Lafitte by informing on themselves
Family turns the Sandbar Fight fame into a knife brand and legend
Years of fraudulent land sales in Arkansas
Forged deeds and hired actors to sell land he never owned
Silver-hunting party fights a multi-day battle with Native tribes, many killed
Monclova land sale in Coahuila, arrest and escape back to Texas
Texas Revolution: elected colonel, wins at Concepcion, revolt becomes secession
Repeated hanging and burning of a captured Mexican man for information
Yellow fever at the Alamo; battle begins and he dies in 1836
Competing myths about his death and the grifters who spread them

notes: Primary theme folklore-legend because the story is framed as the real man behind the frontier hero; fraud-grift was a close alternative. Texas Revolution tagged civil-war as a secession inside Mexico. Lafitte's dates are approximate. Bear-trap hunting account is short but vivid, hence animal-cruelty. The Native fight is not narrated in detail, so no mass-atrocity.
